# Linkedin.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/linkedin-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/linkedin-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects data from linkedin.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape LinkedIn in 2025](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-linkedin)
- **Code:** [`linkedin.py`](linkedin.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Profile pages](results/profile.json) · [Company pages](results/company.json) · [Job search pages](results/job_search.json) · [Job pages](results/jobs.json) · [Article pages](results/articles.json)

## What it scrapes

- Linkedin public profile pages for profile data
- Linkedin company pages for company data
- Linkedin job search pages for job data
- Linkedin job pages for detailed job data
- Linkedin article pages for article data

## Functions

- `scrape_profile(urls)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape public linkedin profile pages
- `scrape_company(urls)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape prublic linkedin company pages
- `scrape_job_search(keyword, location, max_pages=None)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape Linkedin job search
- `scrape_jobs(urls)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape Linkedin job pages
- `scrape_articles(urls)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape Linkedin articles

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import linkedin


async def main():
    profile = await linkedin.scrape_profile(urls=["https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates"])
    company = await linkedin.scrape_company(
        urls=[
            "https://linkedin.com/company/microsoft",
            "https://linkedin.com/company/google",
        ],
    )
    job_search = await linkedin.scrape_job_search(
        keyword="Python Developer",
        location="United States",
        max_pages=3,
    )
    articles = await linkedin.scrape_articles(
        urls=[
            "https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/last-chapter-my-career-bill-gates-tvlnc",
            "https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/drone-didis-taking-flight-bill-gates-b1okc",
        ],
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/profile.json`](results/profile.json): `profile`, `posts`
- [`results/company.json`](results/company.json): `overview`, `life`
- [`results/job_search.json`](results/job_search.json): `title`, `company`, `address`, `timeAdded`, `jobUrl`, `companyUrl`
- [`results/jobs.json`](results/jobs.json): `@context`, `@type`, `datePosted`, `employmentType`, `hiringOrganization`, `identifier`, `image`, `industry`, `jobLocation`, `skills`, `title`, `validThrough`, `educationRequirements`, `experienceRequirements`, `jobDescription`
- [`results/articles.json`](results/articles.json): `@context`, `@type`, `headline`, `url`, `publisher`, `name`, `commentCount`, `interactionStatistic`, `datePublished`, `mainEntityOfPage`, `isAccessibleForFree`, `image`, `dateModified`, `author`, `articleBody`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`linkedin.py`](linkedin.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy
- `headers` = `{"Accept-Language": "en-US,en;q=0.5"}`
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/linkedin-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_profile_scraping`, `test_company_scraping`, `test_job_search_scraping`, `test_job_page_scraping`, `test_article_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
